name: Outlook & Exchange Online
summary: Microsoft's hosted mailboxes, calendars and contacts, and the Outlook client that goes with them.

factors: An @outlook.com or @hotmail.com address belongs to Microsoft and cannot move with you
Shared mailboxes, delegated calendars, room booking and distribution groups
Meeting invitations and free/busy lookups that assume everyone is on Exchange
Password login for IMAP is switched off, so third-party tools must use modern authentication
Years of mail in online archives and .pst files

export.summary: Mail comes out over IMAP or as .pst archives; calendars and contacts export as .ics and .csv. Rules, delegation and shared-mailbox permissions do not export at all.

methods.name: IMAP sync
methods.detail: Use imapsync, or your new server's built-in sync jobs, to copy each mailbox folder by folder to the new server. Exchange Online requires OAuth2 rather than a password.

methods.name: PST export
methods.detail: Outlook for Windows exports a mailbox to a .pst file, and administrators can export in bulk through Microsoft Purview. The readpst tool (libpst) converts .pst to mbox for other clients.

methods.name: Calendar and contacts
methods.detail: Export calendars as .ics and contacts as .csv or vCard, then import them into your new calendar and address book.

caveats: If your address is @outlook.com or @hotmail.com, set up forwarding and change your address everywhere gradually
Recurring meetings that you organise must be sent again from the new calendar
Inbox rules, categories and signatures have to be recreated
Lower the DNS TTL on your MX records a few days before switching, so that the change takes effect quickly

paths.verdict: The lowest-risk first step: change the client now, keep the mailbox, and move the server later, or never.

import.summary: Add the account and your mail appears, using Thunderbird's native Exchange support or IMAP with modern authentication. Local .pst archives need converting unless you import on a Windows machine that still has Outlook installed.

transfers: All mail and folders held on the server
Several accounts in one unified inbox
Calendars and contacts, directly or after an export
lost: Teams and Office integration, such as meeting buttons and presence
Shared-calendar conveniences that depend on Exchange

paths.verdict: For organisations that own their domain and have someone willing to run a mail server properly.

import.summary: Create the mailboxes, then use mailcow's built-in sync jobs to pull each one across over IMAP. Run both systems in parallel, switch the MX records, and sync once more to catch stragglers.

transfers: Calendars and contacts, after export and import
Phone and Outlook sync over ActiveSync
lost: Shared-mailbox permissions and delegation, which you recreate by hand
Microsoft's sending reputation: yours starts from zero
Compliance features such as retention policies and eDiscovery

paths.verdict: A lean, modern server for technically confident teams who are happy to use standard mail clients.

import.summary: Create the accounts, copy mailboxes across with imapsync, import calendars and contacts over CalDAV and CardDAV, then switch the MX records.

transfers: Calendars and contacts, after export and import
lost: ActiveSync: phones and Outlook connect over IMAP, CalDAV and CardDAV instead
Shared-mailbox permissions and delegation, which you recreate by hand
Microsoft's sending reputation: yours starts from zero
